tagline: Across marshes and Lemon Island toward the Broad River crossing
intro: SC 170’s scenic stretch runs from SC 462 to the south side of the Broad River, crossing the Chechesee River and Lemon Island. Marshes and islands spread beside the road after the Callawassie Island turnoff. The General Assembly designated this section a state scenic highway in 2012. The Chechesee crossing carries four lanes, and the road briefly becomes divided as it winds southeast across Lemon Island. The Broad River crossing beyond is also four lanes, linking the northern and southern parts of Beaufort County.

The route toward Beaufort took its present direction in 1958, when SC 170 was rerouted over the Broad River Bridge to U.S. 21. Its old route north through Coosawhatchie became SC 462. Growth pressures and safety concerns later prompted a larger, taller fixed bridge to replace the two-lane drawbridge. The four-lane replacement was completed in 2004. Parts of the former drawbridge became a county fishing dock.

From the SC 462 junction near Okatie, head east along a road that follows portions of the Jasper–Beaufort county line. After the Callawassie turnoff, continue over the Chechesee River and southeast across Lemon Island. The scenic designation ends at the Broad River’s south side; SC 170 continues across the bridge toward Burton.

moments.title: Okatie
moments.text: Okatie takes its name from the Okatee River, an estuary of Port Royal Sound. The community stretches across parts of Jasper and Beaufort counties, between I-95 and SC 462. It was designated a voting precinct in 1916 and remains unincorporated. Since the 1990s, residential development has included Sun City Hilton Head, Riverbend and Oldfield.

moments.title: Chechesee River and Lemon Island
moments.text: The Chechesee River bridge carries four lanes onto Lemon Island, with the Edgar C. Glenn Boat Ramp underneath. Across the island, SC 170 winds southeast toward the Broad River. Its divided section is brief: the median gives way before the highway leaves the island. The approach from the Callawassie turnoff brings views across marshes and surrounding islands.

moments.title: Broad River Bridge
moments.text: The Broad River crossing changed from a two-lane drawbridge to a taller fixed span as growth and safety concerns demanded more capacity. Completed in 2004, the replacement carries four lanes of SC 170 between northern and southern Beaufort County. It is 1.7 miles long and also bears the name Edward Burton Rogers Bridge. Beaufort County bought portions of the former bridge for a fishing dock. The old crossing’s remains lie north of the present bridge. On the far side of the crossing, the highway enters Burton and takes the name Robert Smalls Parkway as it continues across Port Royal Island.
moments.notice: The former drawbridge’s remains sit north of the current crossing.

sources.label: South Carolina Legislature, Code of Laws, Title 57 Chapter 23
